long_description.before:
We build collaborative robot squads for solar farm construction.

High labor costs, labor shortages, and unpredictable productivity make infrastructure difficult to build in places that are remote, harsh, or empty. We are building robots to unlock places once considered too difficult to develop. Solar is our first proving ground, spanning utility-scale, commercial and industrial, community solar, agrivoltaic, and other projects.

Unlike solutions that automate only one task, or even part of one, we cover the workflow after PV module pallets arrive on-site: transportation, installation, alignment, and fastening. Each robot has a specific role, and fleets can be configured based on each project’s cost and schedule requirements.

Our robots operate autonomously with remote supervision. One person can supervise 4+ robots through a screen and an e-stop button, without being physically present or teleoperating them. Our robotic fleet has also been tested at night, paving the way for 24/7 operation.

We work directly with EPCs through a Robotics-as-a-Service model, requiring no robot purchase or large upfront capital investment. We also work with racking and PV module manufacturers to certify compatibility and give customers confidence in deployment.

Purpose-built hardware, multimodal sensing, and physical AI software help our robots handle real-world construction uncertainty.

long_description.before:
WithAI helps institutional investors research stocks and manage their portfolios. We're live with four hedge funds, and our users spend 4+ hours a day in the platform.

Investors who try "nearly every tool on the market," to quote a client of ours, "wind up with an unwieldy collection of fragmented point solutions." Those who focus on building a great setup with general agents are instead "signing up for a full-time job." So we deploy a platform called Multiplier that unifies structured data, unstructured data, AI work, human work, and tacit firm knowledge in one secure, governed, customized application.

Our first vertical: independent equity funds with $250M-$5B of assets. They know AI is essential for staying relevant, but they don't have the time or talent to figure out what to do about it. But once we deploy Multiplier––"We used to spend 80% of our time gathering information and 20% of our time acting on it," said one customer. "WithAI has flipped those percentages."

Speko is a router for voice models: one API key, and your voice agent runs on the speech-to-text, LLM, and text-to-speech models we measured as best for your language and use case. The measurements are public at benchmarks.speko.ai: we test new models the day they ship and re-route when the numbers change, so you rewrite nothing. long_description.before: IMPACT builds autonomous interceptor drones that ship in a sealed box. The box sits at the site it protects (data centers, power grid, airports, bases) with no crew on the pad. When sensors cue a hostile drone, an interceptor pierces its own frangible lid, launches, and rams the target, guided by onboard visual navigation that keeps working when GPS is jammed. Legacy effectors cost $1M+ per shot against $30k threats; our interceptors cost like the threat and launches scale with the swarm. Sites subscribe to protection instead of buying missiles: hardware, reloads, and monitoring included. Air defense as a Service.
long_description.after: IMPACT builds autonomous interceptor drones that ship in sealed containers. The box sits at the site it protects, data centers, power grids, airports, bases, with no crew on the pad. Lyon builds private foundation models for banks, insurance companies, and fintechs. Each model learns from the company’s proprietary transactions, payments, clicks, and customer interactions to predict credit, fraud, collections, income, churn, and lifetime value; and runs inside the company’s cloud, so its data and intelligence remain under its control. Lyon is already working with a major insurer and trained a model on 28B transactions for a fintech serving tens of millions of active users, identifying premium-card converters 4x more precisely than its existing rules; the model is now being deployed for credit.

long_description.before:
Floracene lets anyone at a medical practice describe the internal tool they need and deploy it in one click - connected to production data, with read and write access scoped by the user. Think Lovable or Retool, except purpose-built for the needs of a medical practice that has no engineering team.

The bottleneck in healthcare isn't building anymore. Anyone can vibecode an 80% solution in an afternoon, custom to their own workflow, with people already on staff. The tool then dies locally on the builder’s computer, because IT (correctly) won't let anyone deploy a tool touching PHI without first-class authentication and permissioning. Our first design partner had multiple employees who had each built useful tools and dashboards locally, but couldn’t actually share these with coworkers or connect to their core practice data. Within weeks of implementing Floracene, they were able to cut a $12K / month contract for a crappy dashboarding tool and had 4 home-built tools shipped to production.

~$200B is spent on administrative software in healthcare every year in the US. Tens of thousands of those companies still run core operations on spreadsheets, and we're at the top of the first inning of AI adoption.

Asaph and Jonah met on the hospitals team at Palantir two years ago, and have each spent the last four years in the plumbing of US healthcare: claims, eligibility, and payor contracting. Asaph was an early PM at Garner. Jonah was a founding engineer at Metriport (YC S22) after starting his own fax-automation startup for fertility clinics.

long_description.before:
Nori builds sub-$2000 bimanual mobile manipulator that can clean rooms, restock shelves, and fold clothes. Nori can handle basic tasks out of the box, and its software lets anyone teach Nori to automate work specific to their home or business. 

Nori aims to solve the robotics data bottleneck. By deploying affordable robots to customers around the world, we can gather the diverse data required to train the next generation of generalist robotic policies. Every user of Nori makes Nori smarter.

Since launching 6 weeks ago we have already deployed our first robot and have 100k in sales.

We can bring general-purpose robotics to homes and businesses that could never afford it before. There are 132.7 million households and 8.4 million employer business locations in the U.S. At $1,688 per robot, selling just one Nori to 0.5% of them represents a $1.2B market opportunity in the U.S. alone.

long_description.before:
Denta saves companies money and time on dental insurance. In two minutes, employers can sign up directly, without dealing with the middlemen who add 25% to the cost.

I started Denta after building software for my dad's 10 dental practices. In scaling that software business to 16k MRR in 10 weeks, I realized I was working on a small problem in dentistry. Existing software sucks, no doubt, but what dentists complain about even more: insurance.

Dental Insurance Companies collect $100B/year in premiums. 25% of that is wasted on administrators, brokers, and c-suite salaries. As the son of a dentist, I will not let these companies burn $25B/year anymore. That money should go to dentists via reimbursements, patients via more coverage, and employers via reduced costs.
